_comment: The wild population. ALL TUNABLE. Positions are absolute world metres; everything is stood on the ground by asking the world (D09). Tuskroot is deliberately absent: it is the evolved form, only obtainable by evolving a caught Mudsnout (D20). Veridian is the future legendary, also absent.
_comment_placement: The playground is 512m on a side (data/config/terrain_playground.json), so everything here sits well inside +/-256. Water species cluster at the pond valley around [-120, 130]. Galecrest and Burrowback were meant for the rocky rise at [140, -90] itself, but that rise's rim is a closed >45-degree band by design (terrain_playground.json: rises are 'the only places the 45-degree slope limit should actually bite') — measured at 71 of 72 radial approaches unwalkable — so a creature up there can never be met, fought or caught. Both live on the meadow at its southern foot instead: the ambush happens on the approach below the danger ground, not on an unreachable plateau. The Bramblebun cluster's nearest edge stays within ~60m of the origin, because the opening walks a brand-new player out to it.
_comment_conditions: R5.3 (D20's deferred schema extension). Two optional per-entry fields gate whether a cluster's creatures are actually present: 'time' ('day' or 'night', checked against world_look.gd's is_dark()) and 'weather' (an array of data/config/weather.json preset names, checked against world_weather.gd's active weather()). Absent means always present, which is every entry but the two below. A gated-out creature is not removed, just hidden and non-engageable (encounter_director.gd) until its condition is true again -- so the practice/aggressor roles, which must always be reachable, deliberately carry neither field.
_comment_meadowhart_sh47: SH47/D42, the `remove dead walking` lever and the `spawn density` one at the same time. A SECOND Meadowhart cluster was ADDED at [30, 95]; the original at [-100, -60] is untouched. Meadowhart is the only rideable Meadows creature (data/creatures/species.json's `rideable` block, R6.1) and it lived in exactly one place, in the far north-west corner, ~250m off every route the chapter's critical path actually walks. tools/_probe_pacing.py priced the consequence: a 624m round trip, out and back over ground with nothing on it, purely to fetch the animal the saddle is for. That is spec Sec17 P7's `dead walking` in its purest form -- and the saddle is a Band 2/3 unlock (spec Sec3: 'riding should become available by Band 3 or early Band 4'), so the trip lands right where the chapter can least afford it. [30, 95] sits on the South Bridge -> Old Quarry leg the player already walks, between the established pipwing cluster at [20, 80] and the trailpup one at [80, 60], so the mount is met in stride rather than fetched. This does NOT make riding free: it still needs the catch, the Rootstone and the saddle craft, all of which are on Sec11's GOOD grind list. It removes the walk, not the work. TUNABLE.
_comment_galecrest_wall1: WALL1, 2026-08-17. The old centre [55,-120] r12 resolved (this file's own seeded `wild_spawn_%d` rng) to home (54.30,-124.15) -- only 3.15m from Captain Halder, a stronghold captain trainers.json hand-places at [52.0,-122.0] with his own real capsule collider (npc_body.gd, radius 0.36m). Every 'phantom wall' the CI-AGGRESSION/OF15/WALL1 investigations chased for a full session was this: Galecrest's aggression chase toward the player runs almost directly through Halder's body and gets physically blocked by him -- is_on_wall()==true because there really is a wall, just not a terrain one. Confirmed directly: tools/_probe_wedge_seam.gd's frame-by-frame slide-collision dump names 'Captain Halder/Body' as the collider on every one of the residual is_on_wall() frames at the old coordinates, and a live failing `smoke_aggression.gd` run (DEBUG_AGGRO=1) freezes at (52.97,-122.28) -- the exact reported coordinate -- oscillating around Halder's position. Moved the centre to [35,-115], predicted new home (34.30,-119.15): 17.9m clear of Halder, 23.1m clear of Burrowback's own radius, worst slope 9.6 degrees over a 3m ring (tools/_probe_wall1_relocate.gd) -- comfortably walkable, still 'the meadow at its southern foot' the placement comment above describes, still nowhere near the closed rocky-rise band. Not a terrain or physics engine defect: BAKE-GUARDS' collision_shape_size fix (16->64, ralph/NOTES.md) was a real, independent improvement and stays -- see ralph/NOTES.md for the post-move measured pass rate.
_comment_ow5d: OW5D, docs/MEADOWS_MACRO_LAYOUT.md section 10.2 and section 5's ecology mapping. Every entry below either (a) moves WITH a relocated feature it was already tied to (the four pond species move with the pond; burrowback moves with the Burrow Warrens), (b) stays put because section 10.2's own table says the lower-fields trio (Bramblebun/Mudsnout/Pipwing) 'stay Band 1 near current positions', or (c) is re-sited by hand against section 5's ecology mapping ('grove -> Band 1 oak ring / Band 2', 'quarry/warrens -> Band 2', 'river -> Band 3 near z~4150', 'upper ridge -> Band 4') because nothing else in the relocation table already pins it. Every re-sited entry below carries its own `_why_ow5d` explaining which category it was read into and why. Two deliberate departures from a literal reading of section 5, both named rather than silently done: (1) Galecrest (the `aggressor` role) was NOT moved to Band 4 despite being an 'upper ridge' species, because `tests/smoke_aggression.gd` hard-codes a ~95m/4000-frame walk budget from the spawn pad to this exact cluster and moving it would silently break that test's timing -- test files are a different task's territory per this same relocation table's own WORLD_EDGE row, so the ecological mismatch is flagged instead of resolved. (2) The SH47-added second Meadowhart cluster (originally [30,95], sited deliberately EARLY so riding's mount is met 'in stride' rather than requiring a long detour, per that entry's own comment) was kept in early Band 2 rather than sent to Band 4 with the 'true' Meadowhart population, to avoid reintroducing the exact dead-walking problem SH47 was written to fix; the ORIGINAL far-flung Meadowhart cluster (which SH47's own comment already called out as badly placed) was sent to Band 4's high pasture instead, which is where section 3.2 says the herd belongs. Ground truth at every new site was NOT re-probed by this pass -- see the OW5D report.
